subject: Information Theory
title: Perfect Secrecy
description: A fast breakdown of Perfect Secrecy for builders.

hook.text: Shannon defined perfect secrecy: seeing the ciphertext gives an attacker zero information about the plaintext.

buildup.text: Formally, P(plaintext | ciphertext) = P(plaintext). The ciphertext is statistically independent of the message.

discovery.text: The one-time pad achieves this. Every possible plaintext is equally likely given the ciphertext.

twist.text: Shannon proved a harsh limit: perfect secrecy requires the key to be at least as long as the message.

climax.text: No shortcut exists. Computational security is a practical compromise—betting attackers lack enough computing power.

punchline.text: Perfect secrecy costs a perfectly long key.

quiz.question: What does perfect secrecy require according to Shannon?
options: A key at least as long as the message
